# Deal Structure & Tax Planning — Step-Plan and Closing Checklist

**Date:** October 3, 2026 | **Status:** DRAFT — PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL (Attorney-Client / Work Product)

---

## PART I — STRUCTURE SELECTION ANALYSIS

### 1.1 Threshold Question: Asset Sale vs. Stock Sale vs. Statutory Merger

| Factor | Asset Sale | Stock Sale | Forward Merger (A/B/C) | Reverse Triangular Merger |
|--------|-----------|------------|------------------------|--------------------------|
| **Buyer tax basis** | Step-up to FMV (preferred by Buyer) | Carryover basis (§ 1012) unless § 338 election | Carryover (unless § 338(h)(10) or § 336(e)) | Carryover unless § 338(h)(10) |
| **Seller tax character** | Ordinary income on hot assets (§ 1245/1250 recapture); capital gain on residual | Capital gain on stock (one layer) | Depends on consideration mix; boot triggers gain | Capital gain; may qualify as tax-free reorg |
| **Hidden liabilities** | Buyer assumes only assumed liabilities | All liabilities assumed by operation of law | All target liabilities merge in | Target survives as sub; liabilities ring-fenced |
| **Third-party consents** | Required (contracts, licenses) | Generally not required (change-of-control clauses excepted) | Generally not required | Generally not required |
| **State transfer taxes** | Real property transfer tax; UCC filings | Usually none | Varies | Varies |
| **Complexity / cost** | High (individual asset conveyances) | Moderate | Moderate–High (shareholder vote) | Moderate–High |
| **S-corp / LLC target** | Clean exit; avoids entity-level gain under check-the-box | N/A for pass-throughs structured as LLC | N/A | N/A |

**Recommended Primary Structure:** *Reverse Triangular Merger* (or Asset Sale with § 338(h)(10) joint election if Target is an S-corporation or qualified subsidiary), subject to final tax modeling.

**Rationale:**
- A reverse triangular merger (§ 368(a)(2)(E)) preserves Target's contracts and licenses without individual assignment, minimizes consent exposure, and allows Target to survive as a wholly-owned subsidiary — ring-fencing pre-close liabilities.
- If Buyer requires a full tax basis step-up and the parties cannot bridge pricing, an **asset sale** or **§ 338(h)(10) election** (for S-corp or consolidated subsidiary targets) achieves Buyer's step-up objectives while maintaining a single level of tax for Seller.
- A **pure stock sale** remains the fallback if Seller refuses to share in the tax cost of a step-up and Buyer's basis differential is manageable.

---

### 1.2 Tax Elections Matrix

| Election | Code Section | Who Files | Deadline | Effect | Recommended? |
|----------|-------------|-----------|----------|--------|--------------|
| **§ 338(h)(10) Joint Election** | IRC § 338(h)(10) | Buyer + Seller (joint) | 8½ months after acquisition month | Deemed asset sale for tax; single-level gain at Seller; Buyer gets stepped-up basis | **YES** — if Target is S-corp or 80%+ subsidiary |
| **§ 336(e) Election** | IRC § 336(e) + Reg. § 1.336-2 | Seller (unilateral) | Due date of Seller's return (+ extensions) for year of sale | Same economic result as 338(h)(10) without Buyer's consent | **Contingency** — use if Buyer refuses joint 338(h)(10) |
| **§ 754 Step-Up** | IRC § 754 | Partnership/LLC (if Target is partnership) | With partnership return for year of sale | Adjusts inside basis of partnership assets upon transfer of interest | **YES** — if Target is a partnership |
| **Check-the-Box (F-8832)** | Reg. § 301.7701-3 | LLC Target or Foreign Entity | At least 75 days before effective date (retroactive up to 75 days) | Converts entity classification; can create deemed asset sale | Situation-specific |
| **§ 453 Installment Method** | IRC § 453 | Seller | With return; elect out by due date + extensions | Spreads gain recognition over payment period; risk: depreciation recapture is accelerated in year of sale | **YES** — if Earnout/note component is present |
| **§ 1042 ESOP Rollover** | IRC § 1042 | Seller (C-corp stock only) | Day before closing (purchase + consent agreements) | Deferral of capital gain if ≥ 30% sold to ESOP and QRP purchased within 15-month window | Evaluate if ESOP buyer or ESOP financing |
| **State Apportionment Elections** | Various state statutes | Seller / Acquiror | Varies | Can significantly alter state-tax allocation of gain; market-sourcing vs. cost-of-performance | **Review all nexus states** |

---

### 1.3 Purchase Price Allocation — § 1060 / § 338 Asset Classes

For any deemed or actual asset sale, the Parties must allocate the Aggregate Deemed Sale Price ("ADSP") / Adjusted Grossed-Up Basis ("AGUB") across the seven asset classes in the following priority:

| Class | Asset Type | Tax Consequence (Seller) |
|-------|-----------|--------------------------|
| I | Cash & cash equivalents | Ordinary income to extent > basis |
| II | Actively traded personal property, CDs, FMV securities | Capital gain / ordinary |
| III | Accounts receivable, mortgages, credit card receivables | Ordinary income (§ 1221(a)(4)) |
| IV | Inventory / stock-in-trade | Ordinary income (§ 1221(a)(1)) |
| V | All other assets (equipment, furniture — subject to § 1245/1250 recapture) | Recapture ordinary; excess capital |
| VI | § 197 intangibles (customer lists, IP, non-competes, goodwill — amortizable) | Ordinary (§ 1245) to extent of amortization; balance capital |
| VII | Going-concern / residual goodwill | Capital gain |

**Action Item:** Both parties must file **Form 8594** (or 8883 for § 338) consistent with the agreed allocation schedule. Mismatches trigger IRS examination flags.

---

## PART II — ROLLOVER EQUITY MECHANICS

### 2.1 Structure Options

**Option A — Direct Rollover into Acquiror Holding Co. (NewCo)**
- Seller receives a mix of cash (taxable) + equity interests in NewCo (potentially tax-free under § 351 or § 721).
- **§ 351 Exchange:** Seller rolls stock into C-corp NewCo; no gain recognized if Seller group controls ≥ 80% of NewCo immediately after exchange. Boot (cash/other property) triggers gain to extent of boot received.
- **§ 721 Exchange:** If NewCo is structured as a partnership/LLC, contribution of appreciated property is tax-free; no boot limitation (but mixing bowl / disguised sale rules under §§ 704(c), 707 must be analyzed for 2-year window).

**Option B — Equity Rollover at OpCo Level (Retained Minority)**
- Seller retains a minority interest (typically 10–25%) in Target post-close.
- Simpler structure; avoids § 351/721 analysis.
- Risk: no step-up on rolled equity; Seller retains minority position in a leveraged entity.

**Option C — Management Rollover / Sweet-Equity**
- Management team rolls a portion of proceeds (often 10–15% of deal value) into NewCo in exchange for a profits interest or restricted stock.
- **Profits Interest:** Granted under Rev. Proc. 93-27 / 2001-43; not taxable at grant if properly structured (no liquidation value on grant date).
- **Restricted Stock / Options:** Subject to § 83(b) election analysis (30-day window from grant).

### 2.2 Rollover Term Sheet — Key Economic Terms

| Term | Market Range | Notes |
|------|-------------|-------|
| Rollover percentage | 10–30% of total consideration | PE sponsor typically targets 15–20% |
| Rollover valuation | Same as deal price ("sweet deal" protection) | No discount applied at entry |
| Tag-along rights | Pro-rata participation on any secondary sale | Essential for rolling Sellers |
| Drag-along rights | Majority can compel sale at threshold (typically 60–70% approval) | Protects Buyer's exit flexibility |
| Anti-dilution | Weighted-average broad-based | Standard; full-ratchet is aggressive |
| Preferred return hurdle | 8% cumulative preferred (if structured) | Negotiated; affects IRR waterfall |
| Management incentive pool | 10–15% option pool post-close | Set aside before rollover dilution |
| Lock-up / transfer restrictions | 3–5 year hold + ROFO on transfers | Aligned with fund hold period |
| Put/call rights | Call at FMV upon termination for cause; put at FMV for good-leaver after year 3 | Liquidity backstop |

### 2.3 Tax Treatment of Rollover

- **Partial Sale / Partial Rollover:** If Seller receives cash and equity in the same transaction, the entire transaction is taxable to the extent of cash received (§ 351 boot rules apply if organized as a corporation; § 707 disguised-sale rules if partnership).
- **Installment Reporting Interaction:** The rolled equity is not "payment" for installment sale purposes; only cash and fair-market-value boot constitute payments under § 453(f).
- **State Conformity:** Several states (notably California, New York, Pennsylvania) do not conform to federal non-recognition rules; independent state gain analysis required.

## PART III — EARNOUT MECHANICS

### 3.1 Earnout Design Framework

| Parameter | Conservative | Market | Aggressive |
|-----------|-------------|--------|------------|
| **Earnout period** | 12 months | 18–24 months | 36 months |
| **Metric** | Revenue (cleaner) | Adjusted EBITDA | Net income |
| **Cap** | 1.0× base | 1.5× base | 2.0× base |
| **Floor / threshold** | 80% of target | 85% of target | 90% of target |
| **Payout curve** | Linear above threshold | Linear | Tiered / hockey stick |
| **Escrow holdback** | 100% of max earnout | 50% in escrow | None (unsecured obligation) |
| **Acceleration events** | Change of control | Change of control + termination without cause | None |
| **Buyer interference covenant** | Strong non-interference; affirmative covenants | Standard | Minimal |

### 3.2 Earnout Tax Treatment

| Scenario | Seller Tax Result | Buyer Tax Result |
|----------|------------------|------------------|
| **Contingent consideration — fixed maximum** | Open transaction doctrine (rare) OR § 453 installment (preferred); gain reported as payments received | Capitalized into purchase price when paid; increases basis / AGUB |
| **Earnout paid in Buyer stock** | FMV of stock is a payment under § 453(f)(6); special rules if stock is "publicly traded" | Stock is treated as payment at FMV |
| **Earnout characterized as compensation** (management retention) | Ordinary income + payroll taxes | Deductible as compensation (§ 162) — **favorable to Buyer** |
| **§ 453 installment election** | Gain deferred; proportionate gain recognized each time earnout payment received | N/A |
| **Election out of § 453** | All gain recognized in year of sale at maximum earnout value (or FMV if not determinable) | Allocable cost basis fixed at close |

**Critical:** If the earnout recipient is also continuing as an employee, the IRS will scrutinize whether payments are disguised compensation (ordinary income, deductible by Buyer) vs. purchase price (capital gain, not deductible). Sellers with capital gain assets strongly prefer "purchase price" characterization; Buyers may prefer "compensation" for the deduction. Resolve in purchase agreement and employment agreement simultaneously.

### 3.3 Earnout Protective Covenants (to be included in Definitive Agreement)

1. **Non-Interference Covenant:** Buyer shall not take any action (or fail to take any action) with the primary purpose or reasonably foreseeable effect of reducing the Earnout Payment.
2. **Accounting Consistency:** Earnout metrics calculated using the same accounting methods and policies as the trailing 12-month period ending on the Lookback Date, consistently applied, with no change in revenue recognition policy without Seller's prior written consent.
3. **Earnout Statement Delivery:** Within 60 days after end of each Earnout Period, Buyer delivers a detailed Earnout Statement; Seller has 30-day review/dispute period; unresolved disputes go to Independent Accountant (Big 4 / National Firm agreed in advance).
4. **Acceleration on Change of Control:** Any Change of Control of Buyer during the Earnout Period accelerates all unpaid Earnout amounts at 100% of maximum.
5. **Separate Books / Ring-Fencing:** If Buyer integrates Target into a larger business unit, parties agree to maintain separate P&L accounting for the Target business for Earnout calculation purposes (or agree on a reasonable allocation methodology prior to close).

## PART VII — KEY RISK FLAGS AND OPEN ITEMS

| # | Risk / Open Item | Severity | Responsible Party | Status |
|---|-----------------|----------|-------------------|--------|
| R-01 | **Earnout metric susceptible to Buyer manipulation post-close** — if Target is integrated into Buyer's larger P&L, earnout EBITDA will require careful ring-fencing or agreed allocation methodology | HIGH | Deal Counsel / Seller's Counsel | Open — negotiate protective covenants |
| R-02 | **§ 338(h)(10) — state non-conformity** — CA, NY, and several other states do not recognize the federal § 338(h)(10) election; separate state gain calculation and allocation required | HIGH | Tax Counsel | Open — state tax model required |
| R-03 | **Installment sale + § 453 interaction with rollover equity** — if Seller receives both contingent earnout AND rollover equity, installment sale reporting may be complex; potential open-transaction doctrine argument | MEDIUM | Tax Counsel | Open — document installment sale treatment in purchase agreement |
| R-04 | **FIRPTA exposure** — if any Seller is a non-U.S. person or non-U.S. entity, 15% withholding on gross proceeds applies; certificates must be obtained prior to closing or Buyer has withholding obligation | HIGH | Tax Counsel | Open — confirm seller nationality |
| R-05 | **Management earnout characterized as compensation** — IRS may recharacterize management Seller earnout payments as ordinary income / wages; affects payroll tax and Buyer deductibility | MEDIUM | Tax Counsel | Open — structure earnout payments carefully |
| R-06 | **Working capital peg and earnout metric interaction** — aggressive working capital normalization at closing can deplete cash that would otherwise improve earnout EBITDA | MEDIUM | CFO / Deal Counsel | Open — agree on earnout-excluded adjustments |
| R-07 | **Anti-assignment clauses in material contracts** — change of control or assignment clauses in key customer, supplier, or IP license agreements may require consent even in a merger structure | MEDIUM | Deal Counsel | Open — consent tracker in progress |
| R-08 | **State bulk-sale compliance** — asset sale structures may trigger state bulk-sale notification requirements to protect creditors; failure creates successor liability risk | MEDIUM | Deal Counsel | Open — applicable state analysis required |
